name: FineVoice
summary: AI audio suite for creators: text to speech, voice changer, voice cloning, speech to text, sound effects, background music and talking photos under one credit-based subscription, with a free daily allowance.
best_for: solo creators, educators and small teams who want text to speech, voice changing, cloning, transcription and sound effects in one subscription, and who use most of the quota every month
skip_if: you need long-form narration beyond the monthly character quota, or you want to publish commercially without paying
honest_knock: Monthly and annual Ultra are different products: annual Ultra is listed as Unlimited for almost every tool, while monthly Ultra is capped at 600,000 text-to-speech characters and 420 minutes of speech to text a month. Speech to text accepts files of at most 30 minutes on every plan. Even annual Ultra keeps one cap, 720 AI Talking Photo Pro credits a month. Unused characters and minutes expire at the end of each month, the money-back window is 15 days, and free output is for personal, non-commercial evaluation only.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-23, re-read 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02 on finevoice.ai/pricing, USD selected) FineVoice has a free plan and three paid tiers. Billed monthly: Basic $8.99, Pro $17.99 (the table offers 28% off the first month, $12.99) and Ultra $24.99. Billed annually: Basic $71.99, Pro $99.99 and Ultra $129.99 a year, which the cards show as $5.99, $8.33 and $10.83 a month. The plans are quotas across a suite of audio tools. In the comparison table, text to speech gets 1,000 characters a day on Free, then 100,000, 300,000 and 600,000 characters a month on Basic, Pro and Ultra, with at most 5,000 characters per input on the paid plans; the voice changer gets 3 minutes a day on Free, 24 hours on Basic and unlimited on Pro and Ultra, on both billing switches; speech to text gets 30 minutes a day on Free, then 120, 240 and 420 minutes. Instant voice clones run 3, 50, 100 and 300. These quotas are monthly allowances on annual billing too: the table's annual view still lists them per month, such as 100,000 TTS characters per month on Basic. Unused characters and minutes do not carry over to the next month, and sales tax may be added depending on where you live. The comparison table now has its own Monthly and Annual switch: on monthly billing it gives Ultra 600,000 text-to-speech characters a month and 420 minutes of speech to text, on annual billing it lists Ultra as Unlimited for those and most other tools. Speech to text also takes at most 30 minutes per uploaded file on every plan, Free included; FineVoice told us on 28 October 2026 that this is a technical limit for all users, not a plan quota. FineVoice told us on 23 October 2026 that on annual Ultra most tools are unlimited, except AI Talking Photo Pro, which is capped at 720 credits a month (AI Talking Photo Flash stays unlimited).

compare_with.name: Murf
compare_with.why: Murf is in our dossiers as a voiceover studio: on 3 October 2026 its Creator plan was $19 a month billed annually. FineVoice costs less per year and spreads its quota across many audio tools (voice changer, cloning, transcription, sound effects and music), while Murf is the narrower choice if the job is voiceover production

sessions.what: We tried to sign up for FineVoice by email on 30 October 2026. Daan entered an address on our own company domain, the Cloudflare check passed and FineVoice refused the sign-up, so we never had an account. Nothing below is a finding about the product itself.
findings: After 'Sign up' the form showed: 'Email verification failed, please enter a valid email.' No account was created.
The sign-up screen listed 2000 Characters for Text to Speech, without saying whether that is per day or per month. The opt-in to AI news, tools and updates was switched on by default.
Our test rules allowed one address and no social sign-in, so that was the only attempt. The reason for the refusal is unknown.
We have no saved screenshot of the refusal; the message is quoted from our session notes.
